subject: Fleet readiness authorization for Airly POC — GPU gating items
messages:
From: Monica Patel <monica.patel@redwood.com>
To: Dylan Brooks <dylan_brooks@redwood.com>, Aditya Rao <aditya_rao@redwood.com>
Cc: 
Date: Tue, 15 Dec 2026 09:12:00 -0800
Subject: Airly POC capacity request — initial ask and gating items

Team,

Airly (contact: Sophie Park) pushed their POC timeline up and asked for a firm estimate of dedicated GPU availability. They want to start a 6-week POC on 2027-01-10 and have asked for a soft reservation while procurement completes. Key ask: 8x A100-80GB equivalent nodes (single-tenant), sustained inference throughput ~8k tokens/s across aggregate clients, peak concurrentk requests in bursts.

Attached: airly_capacity_request.xlsx and a rough SOW estimate.

Can you confirm:
- current free pool in us-west1 that can satisfy 8x A100-80GB (or acceptable equivalent) starting Jan 10
- whether we can place a provisional hold (soft-hold, non-billable) until 2027-01-25 while legal/procurement finalizes
- fallback variants we can offer if we cannot guarantee full A100 capacity (quantized 8-bit, mixed-precision on L40s, or split model serving across instance types)

Please call out any conflicting late-stage commitments so sales can prioritize. I want a short, factual reply by EOD tomorrow so I can update Lauren and Sophie.

Thanks,
Monica
Monica Patel
Enterprise Sales
Redwood Inference
monica.patel@redwood.com
+1 (415) 555-0148

Attachments: airly_capacity_request.xlsx, airly_sow_estimate.pdf

From: Dylan Brooks <dylan_brooks@redwood.com>
To: Monica Patel <monica.patel@redwood.com>, Aditya Rao <aditya_rao@redwood.com>
Date: Wed, 16 Dec 2026 11:05:00 -0800
Subject: Re: Airly POC capacity request — initial ask and gating items

Monica / Aditya,

Inventory quick-scan attached (inventory_snapshot_20261215.csv). Short answer: we have raw capacity but with caveats. Current free pool in us-west1 shows ~12 GPUs equivalent to A100-80GB if we reconfigure some reserved instances. However, there are two near-term commitments across Q1: NebulaSys ramp (pre-committed 6 GPUs Jan-Feb) and a small internal infra test that uses 2 GPUs from the same cluster. If we reassign, net available without breaking existing reserved SLAs is ~8 GPUs but it will remove buffer for unexpected spikes.

Options:
- Soft-hold 8 GPUs in us-west1 for Airly from Jan10-Jan25 (no billing) — requires approval from Sales leadership to mark as provisional reserve (JIRA SUP-4123 created).
- If we need to be conservative, reserve 4 A100-80GB + 4 quantized L40-style instances (lower mem but significantly cheaper) and offer hybrid plan to Airly. Latency impact expected ~5-15% on tail p99 under burst.

Operational notes: autoscaler rules must lock min-capacity and we should disable opportunistic reclaim for the reserved set. If approved, I will open a capacity ticket to tag the nodes and update the allocation matrix.

-Dylan
Dylan Brooks
Capacity Planning Lead, Serving Runtime
dylan_brooks@redwood.com

Attachment: inventory_snapshot_20261215.csv
References: JIRA SUP-4123

From: Aditya Rao <aditya_rao@redwood.com>
To: Monica Patel <monica.patel@redwood.com>, Dylan Brooks <dylan_brooks@redwood.com>
Cc: Lauren Bishop <lauren_bishop@redwood.com>
Date: Thu, 17 Dec 2026 08:34:00 -0800
Subject: Re: Airly POC capacity request — initial ask and gating items

Thanks for the scan, Dylan. A couple of concerns from infra/ops perspective:

1) NebulaSys commitment is firm and has SLA penalties if we cannibalize without notice. If we grant Airly a provisional 8-GPU hold we must either: a) get explicit sign-off on contingency SLA credits or b) offer a hybrid variant to Airly that accepts mixed instance flavors.

2) We should only soft-hold for a maximum window. Suggested approach: authorize a provisional hold through 2027-01-25, after which a commit (paid or cancel) decision is required. That reduces risk of long tail usage blocking other deals.

3) Fallback guidance to Sales to share with customer: quantized/8-bit variant will reduce memory footprint but may need model re-compilation and could increase tail latency. We should include expected perf delta and an estimate for a quick recompile run (2-3 days) in the SOW.

Lauren — tagging you for approval on provisional hold window and authorization to mark nodes as soft-reserved. If granted, Ops will apply the hold and note the fallback variants in the customer SOW.

-Aditya
Aditya Rao
Head of Infrastructure Optimization
aditya_rao@redwood.com

From: Lauren Bishop <lauren_bishop@redwood.com>
To: Monica Patel <monica.patel@redwood.com>, Aditya Rao <aditya_rao@redwood.com>, Dylan Brooks <dylan_brooks@redwood.com>
Date: Fri, 18 Dec 2026 16:04:00 -0800
Subject: Re: Airly POC capacity request — initial ask and gating items

Monica / Aditya / Dylan,

Approved: mark 8 GPUs as provisional hold in us-west1 from 2027-01-10 through 2027-01-25. Ops: please tag the nodes and add the SUP-4123 note. Finance/sales ops — prepare a one-page provisional reservation agreement (non-billable) for Sophie by EOD Monday that outlines the hold window, fallback options, and an explicit expiration/cancel date.

Monica — once the one-pager is ready, please share with Sophie and loop in sales_ops@airly.ai. Tell them we will need a signed confirmation by Jan 20 to extend beyond Jan 25 or to convert to a paid reservation. Mention the hybrid fallback option as discussed.

If NebulaSys shift looks likely, Ops to propose alternate placement within 48 hours.

Thanks — Lauren
Lauren Bishop
Senior Director, Enterprise Sales
lauren_bishop@redwood.com
